summary.one_liner: Wazuh is a free and open source security platform for threat prevention, detection, and response, combining endpoint agents with a management server and the Wazuh Indexer/WUI for alert search and visualization.
summary.what_it_does: Wazuh deploys an endpoint security agent on monitored systems, and a management server collects and analyzes the data the agents gather, with the Wazuh Indexer providing search and a web user interface for navigating alerts. The README describes capabilities including signature-based intrusion detection, log data analysis with rule-based alerting (and syslog intake when no agent is present), file integrity monitoring, vulnerability detection by correlating software inventory with CVE databases, and configuration assessment against security policies and hardening guides. It also covers incident response with active responses and remote command execution on agents, cloud monitoring via integration modules for AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, and Docker host and container monitoring. The repository also links to automation tools for AWS CloudFormation, Ansible, Chef, Puppet, Kubernetes, BOSH and SaltStack.
use_cases: detect intrusions and malware on servers
monitor and analyze system and application logs
find vulnerable software via CVE correlation
security monitoring of Docker containers and cloud accounts
meet PCI DSS or GDPR reporting requirements
how_to_run: See the Wazuh installation guide linked in the README for setup
Deploy agents to monitored systems and connect them to the management server
notable: Agent and manager architecture with integrated Wazuh Indexer search and dashboard UI
Signature-based intrusion detection using a regular expression engine on collected logs
Automation tooling maintained by the Wazuh team for AWS, Ansible, Chef, Puppet, Kubernetes, BOSH and Salt
Derived from the OSSEC project; engine component under AGPLv3 while most code is GPLv2
